ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a triangle, with the base labeled 6 cm. A pink dashed perpendicular line is drawn from the vertex to the base, and the height is labeled 4 cm. There is a right-angle mark where the perpendicular intersects the base, and there are identical tick marks on the left and right parts of the base, indicating that these two parts are equal. Reasoning: Because the total base length is 6 cm and it is bisected by the height, each half of the base is 3 cm. Take one of the right triangles formed by the height; its two legs are 3 cm and 4 cm, respectively, so the hypotenuse is sqrt(3^2+4^2)=sqrt(9+16)=5 cm. The left and right slanted sides are equal, and both are 5 cm. The perimeter of the triangle is 5+5+6=16 cm. To the nearest tenth, it is still 16.0, but the standard answer can be written as 16.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a triangle with base labeled 6 cm and a dashed perpendicular height labeled 4 cm from the top vertex to the base. The equal tick marks on the two base segments show the altitude meets the midpoint of the base, so each half of the base is 3 cm. Use one of the right triangles formed by the altitude: legs are 3 cm and 4 cm, so the slanted side is sqrt(3^2+4^2)=5 cm. Since the altitude bisects the base in this symmetric triangle, both slanted sides are 5 cm. Add all outer sides for the perimeter: 5+5+6=16, then round if needed.
